title: Proactive probe fallback orchestrator with tenant-priority skew
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description:
Background:
Customers hit transient 429 spikes and occasional model timeouts in certain regions during traffic bursts. Current reactive circuit-breakers rely on aggregated error windows which can cause slow or overly aggressive fallbacks for high-value tenants. Goal: implement a proactive probe-driven fallback orchestrator that (1) performs lightweight periodic probes to candidate fallback model variants and endpoints, (2) weighs decisions using tenant-priority skew and SLA tier, and (3) triggers soft-circuit state transitions with graded hysteresis instead of binary cuts.

Scope:
- Design probe health signals and scheduling (adaptive frequency based on traffic & historical stability).
- Implement tenant-priority weighting so higher-paying customers get preferential probe freshness and softer degradation paths.
- Integrate with existing routing controller to trigger candidate model variant fallbacks and staged rate decays.
- Emit decision telemetry for auditability and post-mortem analysis.

Non-goals:
- Replacing global circuit-breaker logic entirely (we will augment, not replace).
- Implementing new UI for this ticket (observability links will surface in existing dashboards).
acceptance_criteria: Probes run at adaptive intervals configurable by region + tier
Fallback decisions recorded in trace and linked to probe evidence
Tenant-priority weighting influences probe cadence and fallback hysteresis
End-to-end e2e test that simulates 429 surge and verifies graceful progressive fallback instead of immediate hard cutover
No regression in p95 latency or token cost beyond 3% in synthetic load tests
Feature gated and deployable behind runtime-1.25 feature flag
tasks: Design probe schema and metrics (probe_latency_ms, probe_success, probe_variant_score)
Add probe scheduler service that subscribes to region/tier config
Extend routing controller to accept probe evidence and compute fallback score
Implement tenant-priority multiplier and config surface
Add telemetry dashboards and alerts for probe health and fallback events
Write integration tests and chaos scenarios (429 storm, model OOM, long tail timeouts)
Create rollout plan with canary, gradual ramp, and kill-switch
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff 1: probe frequency vs additional load. We prioritize lightweight probes (short context lengths, cached KV keys) to minimize extra cost.
Tradeoff 2: biasing towards high-priority tenants could starve best-effort tenants during sustained incidents. Mitigation: enforce a global probe budget and minimum fallback floor per tier.
Tradeoff 3: False positives from transient probe failures. Solution: use exponential backoff and multi-probe confirmation before escalation to a hard circuit state.
Open question: whether probe evidence should persist in long-term storage for compliance. For now we log traces and aggregated metrics only.
Perf target: additional CPU usage on routing plane < 8% at peak for medium clusters.
telemetry_and_queries: SLO checks: query probe_success_rate_by_region(): alert if < 95% for 5m
Investigation query: SELECT count(*) FROM fallback_events WHERE reason IN ("probe_failed") GROUP BY tenant_id LIMIT 50
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize probe schema, config knobs, and tenant-priority multiplier (design doc linked)
Week 2: implement probe scheduler and minimal probe client; unit tests
Week 3: wire probe signals into routing controller; implement graded hysteresis
Week 4: integration tests, perf runs, dashboarding and alerts
Week 5: canary rollout to 10% of traffic, monitor for 48h, iterate
Rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with kill-switch at each stage
